meta.title: Multi-Key Orchestrator
meta.description: Pools several API keys per provider, spreads concurrent requests across them under a per-provider, per-model and per-key concurrency cap with one slot reserved for the main process, recovers from 429 responses by rotating keys, and shows a per-key balance card.

ui.panel.title: Multi-Key Orchestrator
ui.panel.subtitle: Version {version} · running since {time}
ui.panel.bypass: When the switch is off, the plugin is bypassed completely and every model uses DSH’s native single-key behaviour.
ui.panel.statusFailed: Could not read the plugin status: {message}
ui.panel.retry.title: Recover a 429 that arrives mid-answer
ui.panel.retry.body: Default behaviour. A 429 that arrives after text has already been streamed is recovered by discarding the partial output and re-running the request; the abandoned attempt stays in the conversation as an attempt record.
ui.warning.quota-check-failed: A balance check could not reach the provider; the numbers below may be stale.
ui.warning.no-header-seam: This provider offers no seam where a key can be swapped mid-request, so a 429 that arrives after the first byte can only be recorded.
ui.warning.correlation-fifo: Request ownership fell back to FIFO correlation: concurrent requests are matched in arrival order, which is less precise than async-context tracking.
ui.warning.lane-fallback: A main-process request borrowed a subagent slot because the reserved slot was busy.
ui.pool.release: Lend the reserved slot to subagents while the main process is idle

ui.rollback.title: Rolling back
ui.rollback.body: Turn the switch off, disable this plugin’s row in the Plugins page, or remove the bundle. The native request path was never modified, so nothing else needs undoing.
